title: Nielsen's Usability Heuristics
summary: Use Nielsen's ten heuristics as an inspection framework; every finding names the violated heuristic and user consequence.

MUST.text: Inspect all ten heuristics: visibility of system status; match between system and real world; user control and freedom; consistency and standards; error prevention; recognition rather than recall; flexibility and efficiency of use; aesthetic and minimalist design; help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors; help and documentation.

SHOULD.text: Record screen/step, evidence, user/task impact, severity and recommendation.

AVOID.text: Do not mark failure merely because a preferred pattern is absent.

EXAMPLE.good: "No save confirmation" cites visibility of system status and notes lost trust
EXAMPLE.bad: "I dislike the blue" with no heuristic or consequence

FAILURE_MODES: Teams often conflate "consistency" with visual sameness; record the specific user confusion.
Missing help documentation may be acceptable for expert tools; validate with task tests.
Heuristic findings without severity or evidence become opinion; require both.

sources.title: NN/g How to Conduct a Heuristic Evaluation
